page: Microsoft Azure F64-32ams_v7 is a compute-focused yet memory-dense instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked up to 4.5 GHz. Configured with 32 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs with 1 thread per core, the system eliminates hyper-threading contention. It integrates an x86_64 architecture featuring modern instruction extensions, including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache per core.

A key distinction of the F64-32ams_v7 is its memory capacity relative to compute resources. With 512.0 GB of RAM allocated across 32 vCPUs, it delivers 16.0 GB of memory per core, which aligns more closely with memory-optimized ratios. The configuration includes no local storage and zero integrated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage architectures such as Azure Premium Storage.

In benchmark testing, the dedicated physical cores yield top-tier single-core performance, achieving 3,789.56 on stress-ng and 40.61 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. Multithreaded execution is similarly capable, registering 118,422.53 on stress-ng multi-core and a PassMark CPU score of 75,667.78. Memory bandwidth reaches 219.74 GB/sec for large uncached block reads and 134.91 GB/sec for writes, contributing to a top-tier PassMark memory score of 2,993.13 and strong database operational throughput.

Cost efficiency is driven by the 1:1 core-to-thread ratio and high memory-to-vCPU allocation, enabling resource-heavy workloads to run without paying for unused execution threads or hardware accelerator overhead. The absence of bundled local disks requires external storage planning, making the instance particularly suitable for in-memory databases, large-scale caching systems, CPU-based machine learning inference, and heavy data engineering pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure F64-32ams_v7 provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. Delivering an expansive 512.0 GB of RAM—equating to 16.0 GB per vCPU—this configuration combines high single-thread compute capabilities with an unusually dense memory footprint. The architecture supports AVX-512 vector instruction sets, 32 MB of L3 cache, and lacks local disk storage or hardware GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier single-core stress-ng scores (3,789.56) and strong memory subsystem bandwidth (219.74 GB/sec read, 134.91 GB/sec write), backed by 89.41 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. With no simultaneous multithreading overhead, this instance provides predictable compute efficiency and memory headroom tailored for in-memory databases, caching layers, and high-throughput data processing tasks.
